Lisa Kudrow :: Career :: 1994–2004: Friends and worldwide recognition :: chunk_0003
Kudrow, the oldest actor of the main cast, reprised the character of Ursula on the NBC sitcom *[Friends](/wiki/Friends "Friends")*, in which she co-starred as [massage therapist](/wiki/Massage_therapy "Massage therapy") [Phoebe Buffay](/wiki/Phoebe_Buffay "Phoebe Buffay"), Ursula's twin sister.[[18]](#cite_note-18) Praised for her performance, Kudrow was the first *Friends* cast member to win an [Emmy Award](/wiki/Emmy_Award "Emmy Award") with her 1998 honor as [Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Comedy Series](/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Supporting_Actress_in_a_Comedy_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Comedy Series") for her starring role as Phoebe on *Friends* (NBC, 1994–2004).[[19]](#cite_note-19) Kudrow received critical acclaim for playing Phoebe. According to the *[Guinness Book of World Records](/wiki/Guinness_Book_of_World_Records "Guinness Book of World Records")* (2005), Kudrow and co-stars [Jennifer Aniston](/wiki/Jennifer_Aniston "Jennifer Aniston") and [Courteney Cox](/wiki/Courteney_Cox "Courteney Cox") became the highest paid TV actresses of all time, earning $1 million per episode for the ninth and tenth seasons of *Friends*.[[20]](#cite_note-20) Phoebe has since been named one of the greatest television characters of all time. She played Phoebe until the show ended in 2004. The program was a massive hit and Kudrow, along with her co-stars, gained worldwide recognition. Her character, Phoebe, was especially popular. *[Entertainment Weekly](/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")* voted Phoebe on *Friends* as Kudrow's best performance.[[21]](#cite_note-21)

During her tenure on *Friends*, Kudrow appeared in several comedy films such as *[Romy and Michele's High School Reunion](/wiki/Romy_and_Michele%27s_High_School_Reunion "Romy and Michele's High School Reunion")*, *[Hanging Up](/wiki/Hanging_Up "Hanging Up

Heidelberg University :: Organization :: Governance :: chunk_0013
The [Rectorate](/wiki/Rector_(academia) "Rector (academia)") is the '[executive body](/wiki/Executive_(government) "Executive (government)")' of the university, headed by rector Prof. Dr. Frauke Melchior. The rectorate consists of the [chancellor](/wiki/Chancellor_(education) "Chancellor (education)"), [Holger Schroeter](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holger_Schroeter "de:Holger Schroeter"), who is the head of the central administration and responsible for the university's budgeting, and three pro-rectors, who are responsible for international relations, teaching and communication, and research and structure respectively.

The [Senate](/wiki/Academic_senate "Academic senate") is the '[legislative branch](/wiki/Legislative_branch "Legislative branch")' of the university. The rector and the members of the rectorate are senators *[ex officio](/wiki/Ex_officio "Ex officio")*, as are also the [deans](/wiki/Dean_(education) "Dean (education)") of the faculties, as well as the medical and managing directors of the [University Hospital](/wiki/University_Hospital_Heidelberg "University Hospital Heidelberg"), and the university's [equal opportunities officer](/wiki/Equal_opportunity "Equal opportunity"). Another 20 senators are elected for four-year terms, within the following quotas: eight university professors; four academic staff; four delegates of the [student body](/wiki/Student_body "Student body"); and four employees of the university administration.

The [university council](/wiki/University_council "University council") is the advisory board to the aforementioned entities and encompasses, among others, the former Israeli Ambassador to Germany [Avi Primor](/wiki/Avi_Primor "Avi Primor"), as well as CEOs of German industries.[[55]](#cite_note-55)

Alaska :: Geography :: chunk_0012
Main article: [Geography of Alaska](/wiki/Geography_of_Alaska "Geography of Alaska")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Alaska_municipalities.svg/250px-Alaska_municipalities.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Alaska_municipalities.svg)

[Alaska municipalities](/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Alaska "List of cities in Alaska")

Located at the northwest corner of North America very near to [Asia](/wiki/Asia "Asia"), Alaska is the northernmost and westernmost state in the United States, but also has the most easterly longitude in the United States because the [Aleutian Islands](/wiki/Aleutian_Islands "Aleutian Islands") extend into the [Eastern Hemisphere](/wiki/Eastern_Hemisphere "Eastern Hemisphere").[[41]](#cite_note-43) Alaska is the only non-[contiguous](/wiki/Contiguous_United_States "Contiguous United States") U.S. state on continental North America; about 500 miles (800 km) of Canadian territory consisting of [British Columbia](/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia") (in Canada) separates Alaska from [Washington](/wiki/Washington_(state) "Washington (state)"). It is technically part of the [continental U.S.](/wiki/Continental_United_States "Continental United States"), but is not usually included in the colloquial use of the term; Alaska is not part of the [contiguous U.S.](/wiki/Contiguous_United_States "Contiguous United States"), often called "[the Lower 48](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Outside "wikt:Outside")". The capital city, [Juneau](/wiki/Juneau,_Alaska "Juneau, Alaska"), is situated on the mainland of the North American continent but is not connected by road to the rest of the North American highway system. The largest lake in Alaska is [Lake Illiamna](/wiki/Iliamna_Lake "Iliamna Lake").

Alaska is bordered by Canada's [Yukon](/wiki/Yukon "Yukon") and [British Columbia](/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia") to the east (making it the only state to border only a [Canadian territory](/wiki/Provinces_and_terri

In 2015, SGCC proposed the [Global Energy Interconnection](/wiki/Global_Energy_Interconnection "Global Energy Interconnection"), a long-term proposal to develop globally integrated [smart grids](/wiki/Smart_grid "Smart grid") and ultra high voltage transmission networks to connect over 80 countries.[[15]](#cite_note-:Curtis&Klaus-15): 92–93 The idea is supported by [General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party](/wiki/General_Secretary_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party "General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party") [Xi Jinping](/wiki/Xi_Jinping "Xi Jinping") and [his administration](/wiki/General_secretaryship_of_Xi_Jinping "General secretaryship of Xi Jinping") in attempting to develop support in various internal forums, including [UN bodies](/wiki/United_Nations_System "United Nations System").[[15]](#cite_note-:Curtis&Klaus-15): 92

After Liu Zhenya's retirement from State Grid, in 2016 [Shu Yinbiao](/wiki/Shu_Yinbiao "Shu Yinbiao") became the enterprise's Chairman and Party Secretary.[[5]](#cite_note-:Leutert-5): 97 Shu continued Liu's strategy of "one special, four large" and instituted a new strategy of "re-electrification" which sought to replace coal and petroleum power with electricity generated from renewable energy sources.[[5]](#cite_note-:Leutert-5): 98

As of 2024, SGCC is the world's largest energy utility company.[[15]](#cite_note-:Curtis&Klaus-15): 92 SGCC is the third biggest company in the world (as measured by revenues) in the 2023 [Fortune Global 500](/wiki/Fortune_Global_500 "Fortune Global 500").[[5]](#cite_note-:Leutert-5): 92 It operates almost all of China's energy transmission network.[[15]](#cite_note-:Curtis&Klaus-15): 92

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fc/Geococcyx_californianus.jpg/250px-Geococcyx_californianus.jpg)](/wiki/File:Geococcyx_californianus.jpg)

[Greater roadrunner](/wiki/Greater_roadrunner "Greater roadrunner") (the state bird of New Mexico)

Owing to its varied [topography](/wiki/Topography "Topography"), New Mexico has six distinct [vegetation zones](/wiki/Vegetation_zone_(latitude) "Vegetation zone (latitude)") that provide diverse sets of habitats for many plants and animals.[[100]](#cite_note-Beck-McNamee-2023a-103) The Upper Sonoran Zone is by far the most prominent, constituting about three-fourths of the state; it includes most of the plains, foothills, and valleys above 1,400 metres (4,500 feet), and is defined by prairie grasses, low piñon pines, and juniper shrubs. The [Llano Estacado](/wiki/Llano_Estacado "Llano Estacado") in the east features [Shortgrass Prairie](/wiki/Shortgrass_Prairie "Shortgrass Prairie") with [blue grama](/wiki/Bouteloua_gracilis "Bouteloua gracilis"), which sustain [bison](/wiki/American_bison "American bison"). The [Chihuahuan Desert](/wiki/Chihuahuan_Desert "Chihuahuan Desert") in the south is characterized by shrubby [creosote](/wiki/Larrea_tridentata "Larrea tridentata"). The [Colorado Plateau](/wiki/Colorado_Plateau "Colorado Plateau") in the northwest corner of New Mexico is high desert with cold winters, featuring [sagebrush](/wiki/Artemisia_tridentata "Artemisia tridentata"), [shadescale](/wiki/Atriplex_confertifolia "Atriplex confertifolia"), [greasewood](/wiki/Sarcobatus "Sarcobatus"), and other plants adapted to the [saline](/wiki/Soil_salinity "Soil salinity") and [seleniferous](/wiki/Selenium "Selenium") soil.

The mountainous north hosts a wide array of vegetation types corresponding to elevation gradients, such as [piñon-juniper woodlands](/wiki/Pinyon-juniper_woodland "Pinyon-juniper woodland") near the base, through [evergreen](/wiki/Everg

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/38/UK_-_10_-_Phones_old_and_new_%282997615876%29.jpg/330px-UK_-_10_-_Phones_old_and_new_%282997615876%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:UK_-_10_-_Phones_old_and_new_(2997615876).jpg)

A man talks on his mobile phone while standing near a conventional telephone box, which stands empty. Enabling technology for mobile phones was first developed in the 1940s but it was not until the mid-1980s that they became widely available. By 2011, it was estimated in Britain that more calls were made using mobile phones than wired devices.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

The **history of mobile phones** covers mobile communication devices that connect wirelessly to the public switched telephone network.

While the transmission of speech by signal has a long history, the first devices that were wireless, mobile, and also capable of connecting to the standard telephone network are much more recent. The first such devices were barely portable compared to today's compact hand-held devices, and their use was clumsy.

Drastic changes have taken place in both the networking of [wireless communication](/wiki/Wireless_communication "Wireless communication") and the prevalence of its use, with [smartphones](/wiki/Mobile_app "Mobile app") becoming common globally and a growing proportion of [Internet access](/wiki/Internet_access "Internet access") now done via [mobile broadband](/wiki/Mobile_broadband "Mobile broadband").

Methionine (abbreviated as **Met** or **M**; encoded by the codon AUG) is an α-[amino acid](/wiki/Amino_acid "Amino acid") that is used in the [biosynthesis](/wiki/Biosynthesis "Biosynthesis") of [proteins](/wiki/Protein "Protein"). It contains a [carboxyl group](/wiki/Carboxyl_group "Carboxyl group") (which is in the deprotonated −COO− form under biological [pH](/wiki/PH "PH") conditions), an [amino group](/wiki/Amino_group "Amino group") (which is in the [protonated](/wiki/Protonated "Protonated") −NH+  
3 form under biological pH conditions) located in α-position with respect to the carboxyl group, and an *S*-methyl [thioether](/wiki/Thioether "Thioether") side chain, classifying it as a [nonpolar](/wiki/Chemical_polarity "Chemical polarity"), [aliphatic](/wiki/Aliphatic_compound "Aliphatic compound") amino acid.

In nuclear genes of [eukaryotes](/wiki/Eukaryote "Eukaryote") and in [Archaea](/wiki/Archaea "Archaea"), methionine is coded for by the [start codon](/wiki/Start_codon "Start codon"), meaning it indicates the start of the [coding region](/wiki/Coding_region "Coding region") and is the first amino acid produced in a nascent [polypeptide](/wiki/Peptide "Peptide") during [mRNA](/wiki/MRNA "MRNA") [translation](/wiki/Translation_(biology) "Translation (biology)").[[7]](#cite_note-7)

It is the [lightest](/wiki/List_of_atomic_weights "List of atomic weights") and [most abundant](/wiki/Abundance_of_the_chemical_elements "Abundance of the chemical elements") chemical element in the universe, constituting about 75% of all [normal matter](/wiki/Baryon "Baryon"). Under [standard conditions](/wiki/Standard_conditions "Standard conditions"), hydrogen is a [gas](/wiki/Gas "Gas") of [diatomic molecules](/wiki/Diatomic_molecule "Diatomic molecule") with the [formula](/wiki/Chemical_formula "Chemical formula") H2, called **dihydrogen**, or sometimes **hydrogen gas**, **molecular hydrogen**, or simply hydrogen. Dihydrogen is colorless, odorless, non-toxic, and highly [combustible](/wiki/Combustible "Combustible"). [Stars](/wiki/Star "Star"), including the [Sun](/wiki/Sun "Sun"), mainly consist of hydrogen in a [plasma state](/wiki/Plasma_state "Plasma state"), while on Earth, hydrogen is found as the gas H2 (dihydrogen) and in [molecules](/wiki/Molecule "Molecule"), such as in [water](/wiki/Water "Water") and [organic compounds](/wiki/Organic_compound "Organic compound"). The most common [isotope of hydrogen](/wiki/Isotope_of_hydrogen "Isotope of hydrogen"), 1H, consists of one [proton](/wiki/Proton "Proton"), one [electron](/wiki/Electron "Electron"), and no [neutrons](/wiki/Neutron "Neutron").

The union's executive branch is organised as a [directorial system](/wiki/Directorial_system "Directorial system"), where the executive power is jointly exercised by several people. The executive branch consists of the European Council and European Commission.

The European Council sets the broad political direction of the union. It convenes at least four times a year and comprises the [president of the European Council](/wiki/President_of_the_European_Council "President of the European Council") (presently [António Costa](/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_Costa "António Costa")), the [president of the European Commission](/wiki/President_of_the_European_Commission "President of the European Commission") and one representative per [member state](/wiki/Member_state_of_the_European_Union "Member state of the European Union") (either its [head of state](/wiki/Head_of_state

1. [Christianity](/wiki/Christianity "Christianity") (76.2%)

Among Protestants, the most popular are [Lutheranism](/wiki/Lutheranism "Lutheranism"), [Anglicanism](/wiki/Anglicanism "Anglicanism") and the [Reformed faith](/wiki/Reformed_faith "Reformed faith"). Smaller Protestant denominations include [Anabaptists](/wiki/Anabaptists "Anabaptists") as well as denominations centred in the United States such as [Pentecostalism](/wiki/Pentecostalism "Pentecostalism"), [Methodism](/wiki/Methodism "Methodism"), and [Evangelicalism](/wiki/Evangelical_Protestants "Evangelical Protestants").
